newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambian premier insurance firm up for sale.
newsitem.headline: Zambian premier insurance firm up for sale.

text.p: The Zambian government has put state-run Zambia State Insurance Corp up for sale in a continued exercise to privatise state-run enterprises, the privatisation agency said on Thursday.

"Offers are invited for the acquisition of 70 percent shareholding in Zambia State Insurance Corp (ZSIC). However, bids for the acquisition of separate divisions of the corporation will be considered," the spokesman said.
The government would retain 30 percent of the shareholding to allow for public ownership of shares in the company.
The company is the largest insurance firm in the country, commanding about 60 percent of the market with annual premiums of over $30 million.
It has a workforce of 905 and has branches with underwriting authority in five major towns, sub-branches in seven others and franchised agents in four more.

"The prospective bidders are invited to use their own expertise to carry out due diligence for a period of four months, and prepare the approach and business plan which will meet the privatisation objectives," the spokesman said.
Negotiations with the lead bidder would be concluded by the end of August 1997.
